title: Sort a stack using recursion
problemStatement: Solve “Sort a stack using recursion” as posed in the A2Z sheet (Get a Strong Hold).
intuition: "Sort a stack using recursion" needs LIFO/FIFO or a monotonic stack/queue. Push when deferring work; pop when the deferred item becomes due.

approaches.title: Stack / monotonic stack skeleton
approaches.idea: Maintain candidates in order; pop while invariant breaks.
approaches.code:
def solve(a):
    # Skeleton for: Sort a stack using recursion
    n = len(a)
    ans = [-1] * n
    st = []  # indices
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        while st and a[st[-1]] < x:  # adapt comparison
            ans[st.pop()] = x
        st.append(i)
    return ans
approaches.dryRun: Each index pushed once and popped once → amortized O(n).

commonMistakes: Storing values when indices are needed
interviewInsight: Amortized “each element enters/leaves once” is the complexity story for "Sort a stack using recursion".
